verification_report.summary:
The entire submitted chapter passes sequential verification for compact connected complex X, arbitrary smooth real theta with PSH(X,theta) nonempty, and every fixed real a<c, under the explicitly accepted manuscript prerequisites. All new deductions were checked, including envelope admissibility, every multiplier-ideal inclusion, limit passages and source comparisons. No BMP/PVP, positive mass, or unrestricted increasing Q-envelope continuity is used.

Q-fixed slices are normalized. Their decreasing endpoint limit is genuine by normalized compactness; nested maximum sets retain supremum zero. The normalized limit is a competitor for its own envelope, while ideal-order monotonicity bounds that envelope above by every preceding slice, proving endpoint fixedness. Left constancy makes the initial supremum exactly Gamma_a. Q-fixedness implies P-fixedness, so the accepted envelope Legendre/Perron theorem applies. The term at a and the cutoff bound give Gamma_a+at <= U_t <= Gamma_a+ct, hence ordinary singularity equivalence at each finite time.

Every transition input is admissible because the background increases. Concavity follows from scaling in the backgrounds (1-s)beta and s beta, followed by addition and order. Projection preserves ideals at every positive weight; uniqueness of fixed representatives within the same background proves transition compatibility and injectivity. Comparing components through eta+eta' proves their common ideal type. A constant base curve establishes nonemptiness, and its projections give the embedding E.

For the retraction, compatibility makes the h/j components decrease. They lie in one normalized lower-curvature class, so they converge in L1 to a genuine potential; distributional positivity puts the limit in PSH(X,theta). If q is this limit, I(lambda q) is contained in I(lambda q_j). Projection preserves the ideals of q, and Q_theta[q] is admissible in every larger background. Ideal-order monotonicity there gives Q_theta[q] <= Q_(theta+h/j)[Q_theta[q]] <= q_j, proving Q_theta[q]=q. The curve properties pass to the limit. Cofinality gives R(S)_tau=inf_eta Gamma^eta_tau, proving independence of h and monotonicity.

The inequality E R<=id follows by projecting the limiting slice in each admissible larger background. For R E=id, the inequalities Gamma_tau <= (R E Gamma)_tau <= Q_(theta+eta)[Gamma_tau] yield, at every positive weight, inclusions between identical outside ideals. The middle slice therefore has the same ideals as Gamma_tau; both are Q_theta-fixed, hence equal. These identities and monotonicity prove the order adjunction and the greatest-realized-system assertion. Realization is equivalent to preservation of the limiting ideal type. The accepted local valuative criterion applies after smooth local corrections and gives exactly the stated equality of pulled-back Lelong numbers. Automatic realization or its failure is not asserted.

The smooth-gauge inputs have the required new backgrounds. Projection preserves the curve conditions and all-weight ideals. Uniqueness in the common final background proves inverses, the cocycle law, system compatibility and commutation with E. The gauge inequalities have constants independent of the perturbation; passing to decreasing limits gives ordinary equivalence to the original limit minus f. Retraction fixedness then proves commutation with R without assuming continuity of multiplier ideals under decreasing limits.

On Kahler X, small multiples of a fixed Kahler form lie below every Hermitian perturbation. A common smaller closed positive form proves independence of the extension formula, compatibility and uniqueness. This identifies indexing collections only. The supplied original SGPT sources confirm their analytic compact-Kahler definition, closed backgrounds, positive-mass initial data and separate projective Berkovich comparison. The perturbation-limit mass formula is also corroborated by [Xia, Operations on transcendental non-Archimedean metrics, Definition 3.9](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Notes/OTNA.pdf). Required arxiv searches and subsequent web searches were performed; exact SGPT statements were checked in the supplied original LaTeX sources.

The raw-volume counterexample is valid: the constant-zero system and its smooth-gauge image both have zero components, while their limits are the unequal smooth integrals of omega^n and (omega+dd^c f)^n. The accepted connected two-torus example supplies these forms. The calculation works for any fixed a<c; the proof's c=0 choice is inessential. Both limits exist, so only gauge invariance is disproved. Manuscript and source files were read without editing.
